proof.text: For every test scheme $W$, a map $W\to Z\times_X X\mathord\prime$ is a pair $z:W\to Z$, $x\mathord\prime:W\to X\mathord\prime$ with $i z=h x\mathord\prime$. The second map is itself a pair $(x,t\mathord\prime)$ with $f x=g t\mathord\prime$; substituting $x=i z$ leaves exactly the data $(z,t\mathord\prime)$ of a map $W\to Z\times_TT\mathord\prime$. The two constructions are inverse and preserve all projections, by the uniqueness clause of [def-pc-fibre-product]. This gives the specified identification with $Z\mathord\prime$. Apply [lem-pc-closed-subscheme-base-change-ideal-image] to $i$ and $h$. Its map is precisely $a$, since its $\epsilon_h$ is adjoint to $h^\sharp$; therefore $i\mathord\prime$ is closed and $\ker b=\operatorname{im}a$.

The ideal $\mathcal I$ is quasi-coherent by [def-sbc-closed-immersion-ideal-sheaf], hence so is $h^*\mathcal I$ by [lem-weil-pbc-module-pullback-quasi-coherent]. Every structure module is locally $\widetilde A$ on $\operatorname{Spec}A$, so is quasi-coherent by [pqf-def-coherent]; in particular this applies to $\mathcal O_Z$ and $\mathcal O_{X\mathord\prime}$. The closed-immersion definition [def-weil-closed-immersion] makes $i\mathord\prime$ affine. Apply the quasi-coherent pushforward assertion of [lem-weil-pbc-affine-pushforward-base-change] to $i\mathord\prime$ and $\mathcal O_{Z\mathord\prime}$ to obtain quasi-coherence of the third term.

Apply [lem-weil-pbc-affine-pushforward-base-change], clause (2), to the cartesian square of step 1 with vertical map $i$ (affine by [def-weil-closed-immersion]). It gives the canonical $\mathcal O_{X\mathord\prime}$-algebra isomorphism $\beta:h^*i_*\mathcal O_Z\xrightarrow{\sim}i\mathord\prime_*\mathcal O_{Z\mathord\prime}$. Identify $h^*\mathcal O_X$ with $\mathcal O_{X\mathord\prime}$ using [lem-weil-pbc-module-pullback-structure-sheaf]. The pulled-back quotient composed with $\beta$ is an $\mathcal O_{X\mathord\prime}$-linear map from $\mathcal O_{X\mathord\prime}$ that sends $1$ to $1$, since the maps are unital algebra maps. Restriction $b$ has the same property. On every open, linearity gives $s\mapsto s\cdot1$ for both maps, so they agree.

source.place: Tag 02KG (lemma-affine-base-change), canonical affine computation; schemes Tag 01I9

proof.text: Fix $V,U,V\mathord\prime$ as in the statement. By [def-weil-affine-spectrum] the morphisms $U\to V$ and $V\mathord\prime\to V$ are $\operatorname{Spec}$ of unique ring maps $R\to A$, $R\to R\mathord\prime$, which make $A,R\mathord\prime$ into $R$-algebras. By [def-weil-closed-immersion], $i^{-1}U=\operatorname{Spec}(A/J)$ over $U$, and by [def-sbc-closed-immersion-ideal-sheaf] its ideal is $J=\mathcal I(U)$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-open-fibre-product] to identify $Q$ with $U\times_V V\mathord\prime$, compatibly with projections; [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra] gives $Q=\operatorname{Spec}(A\otimes_RR\mathord\prime)$. Let $p_Z:Z\mathord\prime\to Z$ and $q_Z:Z\mathord\prime\to T\mathord\prime$ be the projections. Since $h\circ i\mathord\prime=i\circ p_Z$ and $(X\mathord\prime\to T\mathord\prime)\circ i\mathord\prime=q_Z$, we get $i\mathord\prime^{-1}Q=p_Z^{-1}(i^{-1}U)\cap q_Z^{-1}(V\mathord\prime)$. Applying the same two statements to $Z\times_TT\mathord\prime$ gives $i\mathord\prime^{-1}Q=(i^{-1}U)\times_VV\mathord\prime=\operatorname{Spec}(B\otimes_RR\mathord\prime)$, where $B=A/J$. The morphism $i\mathord\prime^{-1}Q\to Q$ is $\operatorname{Spec}$ of a unique ring map [def-weil-affine-spectrum]; composing with the projections and using the fibre-product universal property [def-pc-fibre-product], it is the tensor of $A\to B$ and the identity of $R\mathord\prime$.

These charts cover: for a point $q\in X\mathord\prime$, choose an affine neighbourhood $V$ of its image in $T$. Choose affine neighbourhoods $U$ of $h(q)$ inside $f^{-1}V$ and $V\mathord\prime$ of its other projection inside $g^{-1}V$. Such choices exist since schemes have affine open neighbourhood bases [def-pc-scheme]. Then $q\in h^{-1}U\cap (X\mathord\prime\to T\mathord\prime)^{-1}V\mathord\prime=Q$. This uses no affineness of arbitrary intersections.

Apply [lem-weil-pbc-module-pullback-affine-sections] with morphism $h$, affine opens $U,Q$ and quasi-coherent module $\mathcal I$ (quasi-coherent by [def-sbc-closed-immersion-ideal-sheaf]). The hypothesis $Q\subset h^{-1}U$ holds by construction. It gives exactly the isomorphism $c:J\otimes_A A\mathord\prime\to(h^*\mathcal I)(Q)$ with $c(j\otimes d)=d\,\eta(j)|_Q$. In particular the map is the one normalized by the actual pullback unit, not an arbitrary isomorphism of these modules.

The formula $j\otimes(x\otimes r\mathord\prime)\mapsto xj\otimes r\mathord\prime$ respects additivity, $R$-balancing in the inner tensor, and $A$-balancing in the outer tensor, since $(aj)x=j(ax)$. Its proposed inverse $j\otimes r\mathord\prime\mapsto j\otimes(1\otimes r\mathord\prime)$ respects $R$-balancing because $(rj)\otimes(1\otimes r\mathord\prime)=j\otimes(1\otimes rr\mathord\prime)$. The first composite fixes $j\otimes r\mathord\prime$; the other fixes $j\otimes(x\otimes r\mathord\prime)$ because $xj\otimes(1\otimes r\mathord\prime)=j\otimes(x\otimes r\mathord\prime)$. Additivity proves both identities on all tensors. These formulas respect the $A\mathord\prime$-actions, so this is the asserted balanced module isomorphism. Composing its inverse with $c$ gives the requested identification.

source.place: Tag 02KG (lemma-affine-base-change), final balanced tensor identity, written out

proof.text: Let $u:\mathcal I\hookrightarrow\mathcal O_X$. Naturality in [lem-weil-pbc-module-pullback-affine-sections] gives $(h^*u)_Q(c(j\otimes d))=d\,\eta(u(j))|_Q$. The unit equation in [lem-weil-pbc-module-pullback-structure-sheaf] then gives $a_Q(c(j\otimes d))=d\,h^\sharp(j)|_Q=d(j\otimes1)$. Substituting $d=1\otimes r\mathord\prime$ from the inverse balanced isomorphism gives $j\otimes r\mathord\prime\mapsto j\otimes r\mathord\prime$. By the projection-compatible affine identifications of step 4, $b_Q$ is induced by $A\to B$, hence $b_Q(x\otimes r\mathord\prime)=\bar x\otimes r\mathord\prime$. This proves both arrow formulas and all the stated identifications without flatness or finiteness.

title: Canonical affine diagram for base change of a closed ideal sequence
statement:
Let $f:X\to T$, $i:Z\to X$ and $g:T'\to T$ be morphisms of schemes [def-pc-scheme], with $i$ a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Set $X'=X\times_TT'$, $Z'=Z\times_TT'$, $h:X'\to X$, and let $i':Z'\to X'$ be induced by $i$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. Let $\mathcal I=\ker(\mathcal O_X\to i_*\mathcal O_Z)$ [def-sbc-closed-immersion-ideal-sheaf]. Use ordinary module pullback [def-pc-module-pullback], its unit $\eta$, and the canonical structure-sheaf map $\epsilon_h:h^*\mathcal O_X\to\mathcal O_{X'}$ adjoint to $h^\sharp$. Define $a=\epsilon_h\circ h^*(\mathcal I\hookrightarrow\mathcal O_X)$ and let $b:\mathcal O_{X'}\to i'_*\mathcal O_{Z'}$ be restriction. Then $Z'\cong Z\times_XX'$ compatibly with all projections, $i'$ is a closed immersion, and $\ker b=\operatorname{im}a$. The three terms $h^*\mathcal I,\mathcal O_{X'},i'_*\mathcal O_{Z'}$ are quasi-coherent [pqf-def-coherent]. Canonical affine pushforward base change identifies $h^*i_*\mathcal O_Z$ with $i'_*\mathcal O_{Z'}$, and carries the pulled-back quotient to $b$.

For affine opens $V=\operatorname{Spec}R\subseteq T$, $U=\operatorname{Spec}A\subseteq X$ with $f(U)\subseteq V$, and $V'=\operatorname{Spec}R'\subseteq T'$ with $g(V')\subseteq V$, write $i^{-1}U=\operatorname{Spec}B$, $B=A/J$. The open $Q=h^{-1}U\cap(X'\to T')^{-1}V'$ is $U\times_VV'=\operatorname{Spec}A'$ with $A'=A\otimes_RR'$, and $i'^{-1}Q=(i^{-1}U)\times_VV'=\operatorname{Spec}(B\otimes_RR')$. All such $Q$ cover $X'$. On $Q$, the section sequence of $a,b$ identifies with
$$J\otimes_RR'\xrightarrow{\ j\otimes r'\mapsto j\otimes r'\ }A\otimes_RR'\xrightarrow{\ x\otimes r'\mapsto\bar x\otimes r'\ }B\otimes_RR'.$$
The identification from $J\otimes_RR'$ to $(h^*\mathcal I)(Q)$ is the inverse of the balanced isomorphism displayed below, followed by the canonical pullback-unit map $J\otimes_AA'\to(h^*\mathcal I)(Q)$, $j\otimes c\mapsto c\,\eta(j)|_Q$, where the balanced isomorphism is
$$J\otimes_A(A\otimes_RR')\xrightarrow{\sim}J\otimes_RR',\qquad j\otimes(x\otimes r')\mapsto xj\otimes r',$$
whose inverse is $j\otimes r'\mapsto j\otimes(1\otimes r')$. In the $J\otimes_AA'$ coordinates $a_Q(j\otimes c)=(j\otimes1)c$, and $b_Q(x\otimes r')=\bar x\otimes r'$. No flatness or finiteness hypothesis is imposed.
